summary: Environment B (Xvfb GUI reproduction) could not be established in this session's container - this is a NEW, real limitation of this container, discovered and controlled-tested during this phase, not a regression caused by this phase's code changes.
symptom: Under Xvfb (:95, 1280x800x24), the CIP main window is created (a real native GTK window titled 'Church Intelligence Platform' appears, confirmed via `xdotool search --name`), but the WebKitGTK webview inside it never navigates past its own generic network-error page: 'Could not connect to localhost: Connection refused'. This reproduces at every retry (6-10s wait) and is a WebKitGTK-level failure, not an application-level one - the app's own log shows normal startup (BSB dataset present, sermon/service/content intelligence initialized, 'built without the `whisper` feature') with no application errors.

isolationTest.method: Before concluding this was a real environment limitation (and not a Phase 3.8.5 regression), the identical Xvfb launch was repeated against a release binary built from the unmodified Phase 3.8.4 baseline commit (bd8b135) - i.e. `git stash` of this phase's two source edits, `cargo build --release -p cip-desktop`, same Xvfb display, same launch sequence.
isolationTest.result: The unmodified bd8b135 baseline reproduces the exact same 'Could not connect to localhost: Connection refused' blank page, byte-for-byte the same failure. This proves the failure is unrelated to this phase's commands.rs/LiveChurchBrain.tsx changes - it is a property of this session's container, not of the code.

troubleshootingAttempted: Set XDG_RUNTIME_DIR to a real, mode-0700 directory (was empty/unset) - no change
Started a real session D-Bus daemon (none was running; DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS was unset) and pointed the app at it - no change

Set WEBKIT_DISABLE_SANDBOX_THIS_IS_DANGEROUS=1 (this container runs as root, and WebKitGTK's bubblewrap sandbox is known to be unreliable for root) - the process exited without ever creating a window in that combination
Attempted WEBKIT_DEBUG=Network,ProcessLauncher + G_MESSAGES_DEBUG=all for root-cause diagnostics - the run was terminated by this session's own execution sandbox before producing log output
likelyRootCause: Not confirmed, but consistent with this container's use of a syscall-intercepting sandbox runtime (gVisor/runsc - present in /etc/hosts as 'runsc'/'vm' entries). WebKitGTK's multi-process architecture spawns a separate WebKitNetworkProcess (and, unsandboxed, a WebKitWebProcess) via process-launch primitives (fork/clone, unix sockets, sometimes bubblewrap namespaces) that gVisor is known to only partially emulate. If the UI process's IPC channel to its own NetworkProcess fails to establish, WebKitGTK's generic connection-refused error page - which names 'localhost' because that is the custom-protocol host CIP navigates to (tauri://localhost) - is what renders for every navigation, including the app's own custom protocol.
priorPhaseContrast: Phases 3.8.2-3.8.4 recorded successful Xvfb reproductions (see pilot-evidence/3.8.2/, 3.8.3/, 3.8.4/xvfb and e2e/ directories) using the identical xdotool/xwd methodology in what the harness represents as the same kind of container. Containers in this environment are described as fresh/ephemeral per session (recreated from a clean image at session start), so this is read as session-to-session infrastructure variance, not evidence that the methodology itself changed or that a prior phase's evidence was inaccurate.
consequenceForThisPhase: Environment B (Xvfb) verification of the operator-visible behavior (Start Listening button no longer disabled when speech is unavailable; input-level text; the audio-start attempt now reaching audio_engine.start() rather than being blocked earlier) could NOT be performed this phase. This phase's evidence for the control-flow fix rests on Environment A only: full green regression (workspace unit/integration tests, whisper-feature tests, Windows cross-compile check, frontend typecheck/lint/test/build) plus direct code tracing recorded in docs/phase-3-8-5-audit.md. This is reported honestly as NOT_VERIFIED for Environment B, exactly as Environment C (real Windows/audio hardware) is NOT_VERIFIED - neither is fabricated or inferred from the other.
